quests.instruction: Every day after school, Anu plays the same song on the piano again and again until it sounds smooth. Which action word is being shown?
quests.hint: She repeats something so she gets better at it.
quests.explanation: Practise means to do something again and again so you become better at it.
quests.funFact: Even famous musicians practise every day.

quests.instruction: Sam reads his notes carefully the night before his science test. What is he doing?
quests.hint: He is trying to understand and remember facts.
quests.explanation: Study means to spend time learning about a subject, often by reading or going over notes.
quests.funFact: Short study breaks can help your brain remember more than one long session.

quests.instruction: The jar is stuck, but Maya turns the lid again, using both hands. Choose the best verb.
quests.hint: She does not give up.
quests.explanation: Try means to make an effort to do something, even if it is hard.
quests.funFact: The word 'try' is in many encouraging sayings, like 'Try again.'

quests.instruction: Mr Rao sends the story to the machine, and the pages come out on paper. What does the machine do?
quests.hint: Ink goes onto the paper.
quests.explanation: Print means to put words or pictures onto paper using a machine.
quests.funFact: The first printing machines for books were invented over five hundred years ago.

quests.instruction: Hana does not use a pen. She presses keys to write her story on the computer. Which verb matches what happens?
quests.hint: Her fingers move over a keyboard.
quests.explanation: Type means to write by pressing keys on a keyboard.
quests.funFact: The QWERTY keyboard gets its name from the first six letters on the top row.

quests.instruction: At the bottom of the form, Dev writes his own name in his own handwriting. What does he do?
quests.hint: Nobody else could write it exactly the same way.
quests.explanation: Sign means to write your name on a paper to show that it is from you or that you agree.
quests.funFact: A signature is one of the ways people show that a paper really comes from them.

quests.instruction: Priya makes a quick, rough drawing of the tree before she adds any detail. Which verb fits the scene?
quests.hint: It is a first, simple version of a picture.
quests.explanation: Sketch means to make a quick, simple drawing without much detail.
quests.funFact: Many artists fill whole notebooks with sketches before starting a big painting.

quests.instruction: The outline is finished, so Leo fills it in with a red crayon. What does he do?
quests.hint: He is filling the space inside the lines.
quests.explanation: Colour means to fill a picture or shape with colour, using crayons or pencils.
quests.funFact: In the United States, the word is spelled 'color'.

quests.instruction: Zoe uses the side of her pencil to make the underside of the apple darker so it looks round. Choose the action word that matches.
quests.hint: Some parts get darker, and some stay light.
quests.explanation: Shade means to make parts of a drawing darker to show light and depth.
quests.funFact: Shade is also a cool, dark place under a tree.

quests.instruction: Ben's friend is carrying too many books, so Ben takes some of them. What is Ben doing?
quests.hint: Ben makes his friend's job easier.
quests.explanation: Help means to do something that makes a job easier for someone else.
quests.funFact: The shortest and most important word in many emergencies is 'Help!'

quests.instruction: The children walk behind the teacher in a line. Which verb describes the action?
quests.hint: They go the same way, but they are behind.
quests.explanation: Follow means to go behind someone or to do what they do or say.
quests.funFact: Ducklings follow their mother in a neat line.

quests.instruction: Meena is first in the line and shows the others the way to the library. What is she doing?
quests.hint: She goes first and the others come after her.
quests.explanation: Lead means to go first and show the way, or to guide a group.
quests.funFact: 'Lead' sounds different when it is a metal: that word sounds like 'led'.

quests.instruction: Mum puts eggs into a pot of hot, bubbling water. Which action word is being shown?
quests.hint: The cooking happens inside the water.
quests.explanation: Boil means to heat water until it bubbles hard, or to cook food in bubbling water.
quests.funFact: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.

quests.instruction: Dad puts a little oil in a flat pan and cooks the eggs in it. What does he do?
quests.hint: The food cooks in hot oil in a pan.
quests.explanation: Fry means to cook food in hot oil or fat in a pan.
quests.funFact: The sound of frying is called 'sizzling'.

quests.instruction: Grandma puts the cake mix in the oven so it will turn into a soft sponge. Choose the best verb.
quests.hint: Dry heat in an oven does the cooking.
quests.explanation: Bake means to cook food in an oven with dry heat. Bread, cakes and biscuits are baked.
quests.funFact: The smell of baking bread comes from tiny particles that float from the loaf into the air.

quests.instruction: Rina uses a needle and thread to join two pieces of cloth. What is she doing?
quests.hint: A needle goes in and out of the cloth.
quests.explanation: Sew means to join cloth together with a needle and thread.
quests.funFact: Sew sounds like 'so', not like 'sue'.

quests.instruction: Grandma uses two long needles and wool to make a scarf, one loop at a time. Which verb matches what happens?
quests.hint: Loops of wool are linked together.
quests.explanation: Knit means to make cloth from wool by linking loops with long needles.
quests.funFact: Knitting was once done by sailors as well as grandmothers.

quests.instruction: There is a hole in Jay's sock, so Mum closes it with a needle and thread. What does she do?
quests.hint: She makes something worn good to use again.
quests.explanation: Mend means to fix something that is torn or broken so you can keep using it.
quests.funFact: 'Mend' is a shortened form of the older word 'amend'.

quests.instruction: Kofi gives the shopkeeper some coins for the bread. Which verb fits the scene?
quests.hint: Money moves from his hand to the shopkeeper's hand.
quests.explanation: Pay means to give money for something you are buying or a job someone has done.
quests.funFact: Long ago, people paid with salt, shells and even cattle.

quests.instruction: Nina wants a new notebook, so she goes to the shop to ___ one.
quests.hint: She gets the notebook by giving money.
quests.explanation: Buy means to get something by paying money for it.
quests.funFact: Buy and bye sound the same, but 'bye' is what you say when you leave.

quests.instruction: The farmer sets up a stall and offers tomatoes to customers for money. What is he doing?
quests.hint: The tomatoes go from him to others.
quests.explanation: Sell means to give something to someone in return for money. Sell is the opposite of buy.
quests.funFact: Farmers' markets have been a place to sell fresh food for centuries.

quests.instruction: Dad hits the nail into the wood with a tool that has a heavy head. Choose the action word that matches.
quests.hint: The tool strikes the same spot again and again.
quests.explanation: Hammer means to hit something many times with a hammer, such as a nail.
quests.funFact: The hammer is one of the oldest tools humans have used.

quests.instruction: To divide the long plank, Grandpa pulls a toothed blade back and forth through it. What does he do?
quests.hint: His tool has many small teeth along its edge.
quests.explanation: Saw means to cut wood by pushing a toothed blade back and forth.
quests.funFact: The past of 'saw' is 'sawed', but 'saw' is also the past of 'see'.

quests.instruction: Mia puts a drop of sticky liquid on the paper and presses another piece on top. Which verb describes the action?
quests.hint: The two pieces stay joined afterward.
quests.explanation: Glue means to stick things together with a sticky substance.
quests.funFact: Some glues are made from plants, and some are made from animal products.

quests.instruction: The tablet's battery is almost empty, so Dev leaves it on its cable for an hour to fill it with power again. What does he do?
quests.hint: The battery needs energy.
quests.explanation: Charge means to put electric power into a battery.
quests.funFact: A phone battery can feel warm while it charges, because some energy turns into heat.

quests.instruction: To use the lamp, Raj pushes its metal pins into the wall socket. Which action word is being shown?
quests.hint: The lamp gets power from the wall.
quests.explanation: Plug in means to connect something to a power socket.
quests.funFact: The shape of plugs is different in different countries.

quests.instruction: After using the iron, Dad pulls its pins out of the wall socket. What does he do?
quests.hint: The power connection ends.
quests.explanation: Unplug means to disconnect something from a power socket. It is the opposite of plug in.
quests.funFact: It is safer to pull the plug itself, never the cord.

quests.instruction: Before making an omelette, Dad taps an egg on the side of the bowl until the shell opens. Choose the best verb.
quests.hint: The shell splits open.
quests.explanation: Crack means to break something open so that there is a line or opening in it.
quests.funFact: A fresh egg has a shell that is full of tiny holes, which lets air pass through.

quests.instruction: Next, Dad beats the eggs quickly with a fork until they are smooth. What does he do?
quests.hint: He moves a tool very fast to mix in air.
quests.explanation: Whisk means to mix food very quickly, usually with a fork or a whisk.
quests.funFact: A whisk is made of looped wires, so it can mix air into cream.

quests.instruction: When one side of the pancake is golden, Mum turns it over in the pan. Which verb matches what happens?
quests.hint: The top becomes the bottom.
quests.explanation: Flip means to turn something over quickly.
quests.funFact: On Pancake Day in some countries, people try to flip pancakes in the air.
